## Solution

**The statement is TRUE.**

**Construction (standard realification).** Every $A \in GL(m,\mathbb{C})$ decomposes uniquely as $A = B + iC$ with $B, C \in M_m(\mathbb{R})$. Define the real $2m \times 2m$ block matrix

$$
\Phi(A) \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} B & -C \\ C & B \end{pmatrix}.
$$

This is the usual identification of $\mathbb{C}^m$ with $\mathbb{R}^{2m}$ applied entry-by-entry, so $\Phi$ is an injective ring homomorphism $M_m(\mathbb{C}) \hookrightarrow M_{2m}(\mathbb{R})$, hence restricts to an injective group homomorphism $GL(m,\mathbb{C}) \hookrightarrow GL(2m,\mathbb{R})$.

**Determinant computation.** It remains to show $\det \Phi(A) > 0$, i.e. $\Phi(A) \in GL_+(2m,\mathbb{R})$.

Consider the unitary (over $\mathbb{C}$) change-of-basis matrix

$$
Q = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix} I & iI \\ iI & I \end{pmatrix}, \qquad Q^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix} I & -iI \\ -iI & I \end{pmatrix}.
$$

A direct block multiplication gives

$$
Q^{-1}\,\Phi(A)\,Q \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} B+iC & 0 \\ 0 & B-iC \end{pmatrix} \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} A & 0 \\ 0 & \overline{A} \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\det \Phi(A) \;=\; \det(A)\,\det(\overline{A}) \;=\; \det(A)\,\overline{\det(A)} \;=\; \bigl|\det(A)\bigr|^2.
$$

Since $A \in GL(m,\mathbb{C})$, we have $\det(A) \neq 0$, so

$$
\det \Phi(A) = |\det(A)|^2 > 0.
$$

**Conclusion.** The map $\Phi: GL(m,\mathbb{C}) \to GL_+(2m,\mathbb{R})$ is an injective group homomorphism whose image lies in $GL_+(2m,\mathbb{R})$. Hence every complex matrix in $GL(m,\mathbb{C})$ embeds into $GL_+(2m,\mathbb{R})$ by the block-matrix construction. The statement is **true**.

### PROOF COMPLETE
